name: Lightbox
description: A full-screen viewer over the scrim for images and attachment previews, with previous and next, thumbnails and one button to close. Pass `modal="trap-focus"` for a file read top to bottom (document mode).

props.name: closeOnModW
props.description: Whether Cmd+W (Ctrl+W) closes the lightbox instead of the browser tab.

props.name: modal
props.description: How the lightbox holds the page while it is open. - `true`: focus is trapped in it and the page's scroll is locked. For an image or a preview that fits the window. - `"trap-focus"`: document mode, for a file read top to bottom (a PDF, a document, a diagram). Focus is still trapped, but the page's scroll is not locked: the document's own body scrolls, and Base UI's lock would only rewrite the page's `<html>` and `<body>` styles under it, again on every resize. The scrim still covers the page. - `false`: nothing is held; focus can leave the lightbox.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the dialog is initially open.

props.name: defaultTriggerId
props.description: ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `defaultOpen` prop to create an initially open dialog.

props.name: disablePointerDismissal
props.description: Whether to prevent the dialog from closing on outside presses. For non-modal dialogs, this also prevents the dialog from closing when focus moves outside of it.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Event handler called when the dialog is opened or closed.

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete
props.description: Event handler called after any animations complete when the dialog is opened or closed.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the dialog is currently open.

props.name: triggerId
props.description: ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `open` prop to create a controlled dialog. There's no need to specify this prop when the dialog is uncontrolled (that is, when the `open` prop is not set).

props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

name: LightboxContent
description: The full-screen layer, with the scrim behind it. Popups opened inside it are drawn above it (`LightboxPortal`). `initialFocus` and `finalFocus` are `false` by default, so focus doesn't move when it opens or closes, except in document mode (`modal="trap-focus"`), where they are Base UI's own: focus moves into the lightbox when it opens (the first control after a click or a key, the lightbox itself after a tap, so a phone shows no ring and opens no keyboard) and back to `LightboxTrigger` when it closes.

props.name: finalFocus
props.type: boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType: InteractionType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)
props.description: Determines the element to focus when the dialog is closed.

props.name: initialFocus
props.type: boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType: InteractionType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)
props.description: Determines the element to focus when the dialog is opened. By default, focus moves to the first tabbable element inside the popup, except when the dialog is opened by touch — then the popup itself is focused to avoid opening the virtual keyboard.

name: LightboxPortal
description: The lightbox's own stacking context, at `z-70` above the page's dialogs and popups: the scrim, the content, and every Base UI popup opened from inside, which Base UI portals into this element by default, in DOM order. A popup's own `z-50` then counts inside the lightbox, so it is drawn above the content instead of under the scrim, and a press on it is a press inside the lightbox.

props.name: container
props.description: A parent element to render the portal element into.

props.name: keepMounted
props.description: Whether to keep the portal mounted in the DOM while the popup is hidden.

name: LightboxBody
description: The scrolling body of a document-mode lightbox (`modal="trap-focus"`), under `LightboxToolbar`: a ScrollArea that fills the rest of the content (`min-h-0 flex-1`) on `layer-canvas`, the toolbar's surface. Pass a `className` for another surface (`bg-layer-sidebar`). It takes the pointer back from `LightboxContent`, which lets it through to the scrim, and never passes a scroll on to the page under the scrim (`overscroll-contain`, also while it has nothing to scroll; `overscroll-none` in `className` also stops the bounce). Every other ScrollArea prop, `render` included, is the area's.

props.name: actionsRef
props.type: ((instance: ScrollAreaActions | null) => void | (() => void | { [UNDEFINED_VOID_ONLY]: never; }) | DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES[keyof DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES]) | RefObject<ScrollAreaActions | null>
props.description: Methods to scroll from code that the container doesn't have natively.

props.name: children
props.description: The scrolling content, in ScrollArea's own container.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Class of a content element around `children`, inside the container: put padding and the content's own layout (grid, flex, `gap`, `stack-y-*`) here, so the scrollbars stay at the edges and the gutters layer is never one of the laid-out children. Only with it, `contentStyle` or `fade` is there one.

props.name: contentRef
props.description: An element whose size is the content's, watched for size changes (such as a hidden mirror of a textarea's text). Without it each element child of the container is watched, and children added or removed.

props.name: contentStyle
props.description: Style of the content element; renders it, as `contentClassName` does.

props.name: fade
props.description: Fade the content out toward an edge that has more past it. The scrollbars don't fade.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: How long the scrollbars stay after scrolling stops, in ms. At least 100 with `trigger="scroll"`.

props.name: onEdgeChange
props.description: Called when the area reaches or leaves an edge, and after mounting when the content overflows.

props.name: onScroll
props.description: The container's scroll events.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The directions the area scrolls in. Content too wide for a vertical area is cut off.

props.name: railInset
props.description: Room in px the scrollbars keep clear at each end, such as a sticky header's height, so they don't run over it. Also settable in CSS, on the root: `--r-scroll-area-rail-inset-{top,bottom,left,right}`, which don't inherit.

props.name: render
props.description: Another element in place of ScrollArea's own `<div>`, as the container (an element or a function that gets the props). It must hold children: the gutters are its first child.

props.name: size
props.description: Thumb thickness: `small` is 5px, `medium` 7px; both grow while pointed at or dragged.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description: The container's: by default `0` while there is something to scroll.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the scrollbars show. They always show while scrolling or dragging.
